evidence.why: On non-iOS/Android platforms (e.g. web) refresh/access tokens and user data are loaded from plain AsyncStorage instead of secure storage.

evidence.snippet: console.warn('Secure storage load failed, falling back to AsyncStorage:', error); await this._loadFromAsyncStorage();
evidence.why: Even on iOS/Android, if Keychain fails, code silently falls back to storing tokens in unencrypted AsyncStorage.
_saveToAsyncStorage persists the raw JWT refresh token (and access token/user data) in AsyncStorage, which is unencrypted cleartext storage.
Sensitive tokens are written in cleartext to AsyncStorage as part of the fallback/non-mobile persistence path.

controls_present: react-native-keychain used for iOS/Android primary path
ACCESSIBLE.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY accessibility flag on Keychain writes
other_classes_observed: client_secret handled client-side in OAuth flows (potential secret exposure)
silent fallback on secure storage failure without surfacing security-relevant error to caller
